body:
The README's federation section still carries a "what channels do NOT do yet" list naming
limitations that landed weeks ago — T197 (sibling lenses), T198 (identical law from two peers),
and T199 (severed-lens fallback) are all fixed on main, with rails. Anyone pitching Loam from
the README will believe the headline two-laptop demo is impossible. Docs describing a WORSE
state than the code delivers are still dishonest docs.

Build: re-verify every claim in the README's federation section against spec/46, spec/47, and
main's rails; rewrite the limitations list to name only limitations that hold, each citing its
open ticket (the operator-token cost of opening a channel — T196/T188 — is the big true one). One
mapping subtlety, resolved here: T196's shard remains open for the credential-location
decision, but its restart-survival half LANDED (#440) — the mapping treats T196 as
open-with-a-landed-half; cite it only for the token cost, never for restart survival.
Check the quickstart commands against the current `loam federate --help` output.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) Every limitation named in the section maps to an open ticket in .adlc/tickets/, and no
    landed ticket is named as a limitation. Verify: review against `adlc ticket list` and
    spec/46 + spec/47; the PR body lists the mapping.
(b) Every command in the federation quickstart matches the current CLI surface. Verify: run
    each against a built CLI using the two-store rig (a second served mkdtemp store as the
    peer — the shape test/federation already uses; the quickstart's literal peer.example URLs
    cannot run as printed); the PR body records the transcript.
(c) The section states the operator-token cost of opening a channel plainly, citing its ticket
    — the honest wart stays visible until it is fixed. Verify: review; grep for the ticket id
    in the section.

Merge tier: docs repair — self-merges on green.
title: README federation section catches up with main
